Data generation is noisy, so even if the model exactly replicates the true underlying function (black line), the noise in the test data (gray points) means that some error will remain (gray region represents two standard deviations). b) Bias. Even with the best possible parameters, the three-region model (cyan line) cannot exactly fit the true function (black line). This bias is another source of error (gray regions represent signed error). c) Variance. In practice, we have limited noisy training data (orange points). When we fit the model, we don’t recover the best possible function from panel (b) but a slightly different function (cyan line) that reflects idiosyncrasies of the training data. This provides an additional source of error (gray region represents two standard deviations). Figure 8.6 shows how this region was calculated.
